title: Psychology: The Big Picture
objective: After this level you can explain what psychology studies, how psychologists test their ideas and what its main areas are.
summary: Psychology is the scientific study of mind and behavior. Since no one can read minds, psychologists measure what they can observe, and the field spans many areas.

cards.headline: Does a bird sing because it's happy? Science can't say.
cards.body: Nobody can measure a bird's happiness, so the idea can't be tested. Yet psychology, the scientific study of the mind and behavior, faces a version of that problem every day. How do you study something you can't see? And why does the field reach from memory to friendship?

cards.headline: From soul-study to science
cards.body: The word psychology joins Greek psykhe, "breath, spirit, soul", with -logia, "study of". So the name promises a study of the soul. The modern job description is more down to earth: psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. The soul part got quietly retired; the curiosity stayed.

cards.headline: Measuring what you can't see
cards.body: Nobody can read another person's mind, so psychologists work indirectly. They measure what they can observe: behavior, biological signals and self-reports, meaning what people tell them. From those, they infer what the mind is doing. That rescues half the bird puzzle: you can't quiz a bird, but you can ask people whether they sing because they're happy. Then psychologists publish their results so others can repeat the test and check.

mascot.line: Keep this one: psychology measures what it can observe and reasons its way to the mind behind it.

items.label: Body and mind
points: Biopsychology: how the nervous system shapes behavior
Cognitive: thoughts and how they guide action

items.label: People over time
points: Developmental: how people change across the lifespan
Personality: what makes each person unique

items.label: People together
points: Social: how we relate to and influence others
The APA, the largest group of psychologists, has 54 divisions

cards.headline: Psychology: mapped
learned: Psychology is the scientific study of mind and behavior
Minds are studied through behavior, body signals and self-reports
Results are published so others can repeat them
Many areas: biological, cognitive, developmental, social, personality

questions.prompt: By today's definition, psychology is the scientific study of _____.

options.label: the soul and its fate
options.rationale: That was the old sense of the Greek name, not the modern definition.

options.label: the brain's anatomy only
options.rationale: Brain anatomy is biology; psychology studies mind and behavior.

options.label: hidden meanings in dreams
options.rationale: That was one theorist's method, not the definition of the field.

questions.explanation: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. Its Greek name once meant "study of the soul".

questions.prompt: Why can people be asked whether they sing because they're happy, when the same question about birds can't be tested?

options.label: Birds never sing when they are happy
options.rationale: Nobody can tell, because a bird's happiness can't be measured.

options.label: Human happiness can be seen on a brain scan alone
options.rationale: Self-report is the measure here, not a scan alone.

options.label: People can report what they feel; birds cannot
Only humans have a mind to study
options.rationale: The problem is measuring the bird's feelings, not whether it has any.

questions.explanation: Psychologists study the mind through what they can observe, including self-reports. People can tell us why they sing; a bird can't.

questions.prompt: Match each area of psychology with what it studies.

pairs.right: How the nervous system shapes behavior
Thoughts and how they guide action
How people change across the lifespan
How we relate to and influence others

questions.explanation: Biopsychology studies how the nervous system shapes behavior, cognitive psychology studies thoughts, developmental psychology studies change across the lifespan, and social psychology studies how we relate to others.
